title: Pandemonium: A Paradigm for Learning
note: Recognition built from many simple, independent "demons" whose outputs are combined, an early modular architecture.

title: STRIPS: A New Approach to the Application of Theorem Proving to Problem Solving
authors: Richard E. Fikes, Nils J. Nilsson
note: Represents actions as operators with preconditions and effects, so a planner can chain them into new plans.

title: A Robust Layered Control System for a Mobile Robot
venue: IEEE Journal of Robotics and Automation 1986
note: The subsumption architecture: robot behavior built from layers of simple, independently running modules.

title: NASA/NBS Standard Reference Model for Telerobot Control System Architecture (NASREM)
authors: James S. Albus, Harry G. McCain, Ronald Lumia
note: A hierarchical reference architecture that decomposes robot control into sensing, world modeling and planning modules at multiple time scales.

title: Sequential Composition of Dynamically Dexterous Robot Behaviors
authors: Robert R. Burridge, Alfred A. Rizzi, Daniel E. Koditschek
note: Chains feedback controllers whose regions of attraction funnel into one another, with guarantees on the composed behavior.

title: Between MDPs and Semi-MDPs: A Framework for Temporal Abstraction in Reinforcement Learning
authors: Richard S. Sutton, Doina Precup, Satinder Singh
note: The options framework: temporally extended skills that an agent can learn, reuse and sequence.

title: Motor Learning through the Combination of Primitives
venue: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B 2000
note: Evidence that animals produce movement by combining a small set of motor primitives.

title: Training Products of Experts by Minimizing Contrastive Divergence
note: Combines models by multiplying their distributions, the idea behind composing energies and diffusion scores.
